about.title: Kerman Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Kerman residents rely on a small network of clinics and Fresno County medical facilities for care, and most visits go as expected. But when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mismanages medication, the consequences can be serious and lasting. California law treats these cases differently from a typical injury claim — there are shorter deadlines, notice requirements, and rules about expert testimony that make early guidance important. We handle medical malpractice claims in Kerman and can review your records, explain whether your case meets California's malpractice standards, and walk through next steps. A bad outcome by itself doesn't mean malpractice occurred, so getting a knowledgeable read on your specific situation matters. Your free case review comes at no cost, and we work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to act. A 90-day pre-suit notice is also required before a lawsuit can be filed, so waiting too long can close the door entirely.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because a bad medical outcome alone isn't proof of malpractice, California requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in on most claims. We can help arrange that review before deciding whether to move forward.

items.title: Understanding the Non-Economic Damages Cap
items.desc: California places a statutory cap on non-economic damages in malpractice cases, and that cap rises each year. Knowing how the current cap applies to your situation is something our team can walk you through clearly.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Kerman?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from when it happened. There's also a required 90-day notice before filing suit, so it's worth getting a case reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does a bad medical outcome automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that not every unfavorable result is the result of negligence. A qualified medical expert typically has to review the case and confirm that the care fell below the accepted standard before a claim can move forward.

items.question: I live in Kerman but was treated at a hospital outside Fresno County — does that matter?
items.answer: It can affect where a claim is filed, but it doesn't prevent you from pursuing one. We can look at where the care happened and guide you on jurisdiction and next steps.

items.question: Is there really no cost to find out if I have a claim?
items.answer: Correct — our case review is free, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if there's a recovery in your case. There's no upfront fee to have your situation reviewed.
